L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. Assocs., 733 A.2d 677, 682 n. 6 (Pa.Commw.Ct.1999) (“The key to determining whether [an alternative dispute resolution procedure] has been waived is whether the party, by virtue of its conduct, has accepted the judicial process.”). 19	shall continue in force for a one (1) year period, and shall be automatically renewed for additional one (1) year periods thereafter unless terminated by written notice from either party to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the initial or any subsequent one (1) year term.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence insuring agreement whose only flaw is the OCR typo 'THES POLICY', which changes nothing; 'subject to all the terms' is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It simply incorporates the rest of the policy and does not contradict the coverage forms (CP 00 10, CP 00 30) or the Declarations.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"'THIS PREMIUM MAY BE SUBJECT TO ADJUSTMENT' is open-ended but the mechanism is supplied elsewhere; no term is genuinely two-meaninged.","reasoning_cat2":"It fits the Calculation of Premium Endorsement (c029) and the Premium Audit condition (c255) without contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"'Insurance at the described premises applies only for the coverages shown below' is a short declarative limit; nothing in it carries two meanings on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"There is some tension with the blanket limits shown in the Declarations and with A.1 Covered Property (c035), which keys coverage to buildings 'described in the Declarations', but no direct contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"A single line stating products-completed operations are included subject to the General Aggregate Limit; terse but definite.","reasoning_cat2":"It interacts with Section III.3 (c244), which makes a separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate the most payable, and with definition V.16.b.(3) (c275) which resolves the overlap; the fit is awkward but harmonisable.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"Standard first-named-insured cancellation right; 'advance written notice' leaves the notice period unstated but the effective date is set by the notice.","reasoning_cat2":"It is duplicated verbatim at c072 and is not disturbed by the Kansas amendatory endorsement IL 02 61 (c185), which replaces only Paragraph 2.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"A precise two-tier notice schedule (10 days/30 days) with no ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"IL 02 61 (c185) expressly replaces this paragraph and adds reason-for-cancellation limits, so the printed text and the endorsement point different ways until the replacement rule is applied.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"'Last mailing address known to us' is a settled, workable formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the duplicate at c074 and with the nonrenewal notice provision (c186).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"Two short declarative sentences fixing the end of the policy period; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Sits consistently with the cancellation and premium-refund paragraphs (c009) and the installment-payment condition (c016).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"'May be less than pro rata' is indefinite about the short-rate calculation, which is a mild vagueness a policyholder could contest.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes the refund basis, so nothing contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"A single evidentiary rule with no ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the identical rule in the nonrenewal endorsement (c186) and the duplicate at c077.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"An integration clause plus a rule that terms can be amended 'only by endorsement'; the two sentences sit uneasily but each is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The policy is in fact amended by numerous endorsements (IL 02 61, CP 01 01, CP 15 56), which is what this clause contemplates, so there is no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"An audit right limited by time; the only defect is OCR mangling of 'We' and 'they'.","reasoning_cat2":"Duplicated at c079 and consistent with the Premium Audit condition (c255).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"The OCR text is badly scrambled and internally refers to 'Paragraphs 1. and 2. of this condition' that no longer appear as numbered, leaving the cross-reference unanchored.","reasoning_cat2":"The parallel printing at c080 states the same condition differently (no paragraph numbering, no boiler/elevator carve-out), an internal divergence between two copies of the same condition.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"Allocates premium responsibility and return-premium payee in two clear numbered items.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the duplicate at c081 and with Premium Audit (c255).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"'Anyone having proper temporary custody' is somewhat vague, but it is a familiar and narrow formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors the CGL Who Is An Insured provisions (c238 c. and d.) rather than conflicting with them.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming provision that a court could read against the drafter, and 'date and time of cancelation' is left to the notice.","reasoning_cat2":"It authorises cancellation for a missed installment without expressly honouring the 10-day notice in c006 or the Kansas reason-limits in IL 02 61 (c185), a real fit problem.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"A truncated applicability heading; there is nothing substantive in it to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"The fuller version at c084 lists the conditions that apply; the two printings differ only in completeness.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c018","reasoning_cat1":"'Void' and 'material fact' are settled insurance terms, though 'material' always invites argument.","reasoning_cat2":"IL 01 60 (c196) replaces this condition for Kansas with a 'we will not pay' formulation rather than avoidance of the whole Coverage Part, so the two provisions point different ways.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c019","reasoning_cat1":"'Beyond your direction or control' is a familiar limiting phrase; the provision is otherwise definite.","reasoning_cat2":"CP 01 01 C.2 (c190) supersedes and replaces the Control of Property condition for townhouse risks, creating two differently worded versions in one instrument.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c020","reasoning_cat1":"A single anti-stacking sentence with no ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against the several Additional Coverages and Extensions declared to be 'additional insurance' (c051, c053), which a court could see as a tension over stacking.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.22},

{"clause_id":"c024","reasoning_cat1":"The division between 'same plan, terms, conditions and provisions' insurance and all other insurance is a classic source of argument about which limb applies.","reasoning_cat2":"It coexists with the excess wording in the Non-Owned Detached Trailers extension (c050) and the CGL Other Insurance clause (c253) without direct contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
